comment: C type definition names. Struct and union names with a body, like `student` in `struct student { ... };` or `DataValue` in `union DataValue { ... };`, including the brace on the next line. Usages like `struct student s;` or `union DataValue val;` stay uncolored. Names introduced by `typedef`, like `PyObject` in `typedef struct _object PyObject;`, `PySlot` in `typedef struct { ... } PySlot;`. Function and function pointer types, like `hashfunc` in `typedef Py_hash_t (*hashfunc)(PyObject *);`, stay uncolored. The builtin grammar has no scope for these names, so the `typedef` rule wraps the whole `typedef` up to `;` and scopes the names being declared as `entity.name.type.typedef.c`. Struct and enum bodies are tokenized by the builtin grammar, so their fields are not affected.

patterns.comment: `struct name {` and `union name {`, a line ending with `struct name` is also a definition, because the `{` can only be on the next line
`typedef unsigned char name;`, `typedef struct { ... } name;` and `typedef int name[4];`, but not function types, like `typedef int name(int);` or `typedef int (*name)(int);`
patterns.name: entity.name.type.typedef.c
